title: A person's later claim match still credits interest above the cash (11.40 against 6.00): mayYetHold's (b) only sees claim matches standing at the pass, so the netting PLB L6's payment is written and later blocks its own take-back
evidence:
Where the flag comes from:
- remittances.ts:1104 sets mayYetHold to unlinkedReversals.has(chain) || caseLineChains.has(chain).
- caseLineChains (remittances.ts:999-1004) holds only chains with a claim match standing at this pass.
- A chain can gain a case-line claim match later without any upload. matchClaimByHand (apps/worker/src/reconcile/manual.ts:132-161) lets a person match any loaded non-reversal claim, even one since reversed. unmatched.ts:182-189 lists every frequency-7 claim with no standing claim match for exactly that.

Why the overstatement sticks:
- packages/ledger/src/interest.ts:364, 385-387 and 392: a PLB L6 never reaches a line twice.
- So a payment written while the take-back chain had no match permanently blocks the later take-back on that line.

Reproduced at 0755a533 with a database test in my clone, using SYNTHETIC LED-24 variants:
1. zz-p-pcn.835 is paired.835 with C's CLP01 changed and REF F8 dropped, so the reconcile cannot place C, and a PLB L6 of -5.40 naming C. After reconcile: interest 0, cash 540.
2. zz-tc-pcn.835 is two-chains.835 with the reversal under C's CLP01, so it links to C. Draws are B +600, C -540, and no unlinked reversal. mayYetHold(C) is false, so B's 600 is written as L1 267 and L2 333. Interest 600, cash 600.
3. A person matches C to L1 and L2 by hand (both no_change), then a reconcile: P's L6 writes L1 240 and L2 300. X's take-back of C cannot reach L1 or L2, which X already reached. Interest 1140 against cash 600, unchanged by further reconciles.

This is the F1 shape: the same 11.40 against 6.00, now reached through a person's match instead of upload order. The texts that say otherwise:
- ADR 0084:133-136 and the interestWrites docstring (interest.ts:331-336) say the interest a take-back is still to find 'arrives with a later upload'.
- ADR 0084:273 and 278 say 'never an overstatement'.
- The test-matrix LED-24 row says 'never above the cash'.

No test covers it. The order-independence property (interest.test.ts:921-943) hard-codes mayYetHold: true on both passes, so the flag never changes between passes. Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-rv-money-1-h1.log. Test and fixtures: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-rv-money-1-zz-h1.db.test.ts.txt, i126d-rv-money-1-zz-p-pcn.835.txt and i126d-rv-money-1-zz-tc-pcn.835.txt.
fix:
Within 10.1's files (remittances.ts, interest-chains.ts, interest.ts), widen (b) so the flag also covers a chain a person may still match. That means a chain with a loaded non-reversal claim that has no standing claim match and that the adjusted-payments query would offer against an open case line (frequency 7 or superseding, not a case line's own claim, a candidate case line by procedure and date; unmatched.ts:182-200). That is the set of claims a person can still match by hand.

Add this shape as a red database test and an LED-24 variant: C placed by hand after the netting check, expecting interest equal to cash. Add a property in which mayYetHold is false on the first pass and true on the next.

If instead the gap is accepted, state it in ADR 0084 D5 and the consequences, the interestWrites docstring, the LED-24 row and the PR description, and get the founder's ruling. As written, those texts claim the outcome never exceeds the cash.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute MONEY-R4-1. It reproduces at the branch head, the defect is in this PR's own change, and it contradicts the PR's own claim that interest is never above the cash.

Reproduction: I ran it in my own clone at 0755a533, which is origin/co-001/ledger-interest-once now. I used the reviewer's database test zz-h1.db.test.ts and its two synthetic LED-24 twins.
- After zz-p-pcn.835, interest is 0 and cash is 540.
- After zz-tc-pcn.835, the draws are C +540, B +600 and C -540, with no unlinked reversal. B's 600 is written as L1 267 and L2 333, so interest is 600 and cash is 600.
- A person then matches C to L1 and L2 with matchClaimByHand (outcome no_change) and a reconcile runs. P's L6 writes L1 240 and L2 300, and X's take-back of C cannot reach L1 or L2. Interest is 1140 against cash of 600, and another reconcile leaves it there.
- The test fails with "expected 1140 to be less than or equal to 600".
- Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-sk-money-R4-1-h1.log

Control: I wrote a variant where the person matches C right after P, before X is uploaded. It ends at interest 0 against cash 600, so the figure errs low as designed. With the same remittances, only the timing of the person's match turns 0 into 1140. That contradicts the PR's claim that the outcome does not depend on order.
- Log: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-sk-money-R4-1-h1b.log

The person's match is an ordinary path, not a test-only one:
- The matchClaimAction route (apps/web/src/lib/routes/reconciliation.ts:214-232) calls matchClaimByHand.
- manual.ts:132-161 refuses only status-22 claims and the line's own claim, so a frequency-7 claim that has since been reversed is accepted.
- unmatched.ts:182-200 lists C as an adjusted payment, with L1 and L2 offered by procedure and date.

Code cause, confirmed by reading the code:
- remittances.ts:999-1004 builds caseLineChains only from claim matches standing at the pass.
- remittances.ts:1104 sets mayYetHold to unlinkedReversals or caseLineChains. At X's pass, C has neither, so B's payment is written.
- interestWrites in packages/ledger/src/interest.ts never lets a PLB L6 reach a line twice, so X's later take-back is blocked for good.

It is this PR's change:
- The base 8a722f80 has neither interestWrites nor mayYetHold. mayYetHold came in 8ea33e13, the F1 fix in this PR.
- These texts all say the result is never above the cash: ADR 0084 lines 129-136, 273 and 278, the interestWrites docstring, and the LED-24 row of the test matrix.
- The order-independence property in interest.test.ts:921-943 hard-codes mayYetHold: true on both passes, so it cannot catch this.

The shape is narrow, which fits should-fix rather than blocking. It needs a replacement claim the reconcile cannot place, a PLB L6 that pays its interest, a later PLB L6 that nets its reversal against another chain's payment on the same lines, and a person matching the reversed claim afterwards.

Cleanup: I dropped tp_i126d_skmoney_1 and removed the clone. The verdict is saved at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-sk-money-MONEY-R4-1.md

title: The runbook guard test finds a lock loop only when RAISE and USING ERRCODE are on one line with no format arguments, so a later lock loop written in this migration's own two-line style escapes it silently
evidence: packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts:75 finds lock loops with /RAISE EXCEPTION '((?:[^']|'')*)' USING ERRCODE = 'lock_not_available'/g. Line 79 says it 'reads every migration that ends a lock loop with lock_not_available', but line 80 checks only that the two current names are found. Checked with node against that regex: the one-line form matches once. `RAISE EXCEPTION '...'\n      USING ERRCODE = 'lock_not_available'` matches 0 times, and a raise with an argument (`'... % minutes', 5 USING ...`) matches 0 times. The two-line style is the one this same migration uses for its preflight raises at 20261110090000_ledger_interest_once.sql:67-68, 71-72 and 75-76. It appears in 13 RAISE statements across the migrations. A future NOWAIT loop written that way would be neither found nor checked against the runbook, and the guard would still pass, which defeats its stated purpose of making sure whoever deploys finds the failure line in the runbook.
fix: Make the detection independent of formatting. Match `RAISE EXCEPTION\s+'((?:[^']|'')*)'\s*(?:,[^;]*?)?\s*USING\s+ERRCODE\s*=\s*'lock_not_available'` across whitespace and newlines. Alternatively, also fail when a migration contains `LOCK TABLE ... NOWAIT` but no lock_not_available raise was extracted from it. Add a unit case that feeds the two-line form through the same extraction.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. The finding holds as a nit. The guard is this PR's own change: commit 9824f4e9 added the describe block at packages/db/src/migrate.test.ts:72-86, and the branch head 0755a533 still contains it. The regex at line 75 is /RAISE EXCEPTION '((?:[^']|'')*)' USING ERRCODE = 'lock_not_available'/g. Run with node, it matches the one-line form once, the two-line form ('...'\n    USING ERRCODE = 'lock_not_available') zero times, and a form with a format argument ('... % minutes', 5 USING ...) zero times. I reproduced this in a clean clone at origin/co-001/ledger-interest-once, under the lock. As-is, vitest run src/migrate.test.ts passes 21 tests. I then added a probe migration, 20261231000000_zz_probe.sql, with a NOWAIT lock loop that ends in a two-line lock_not_available raise whose message is not in the runbook. The test still passed 21 of 21, so the probe was never checked. Rewriting the same raise on one line as a control gave 1 failed, the runbook-quote case for the probe. The case named 'reads every migration that ends a lock loop with lock_not_available' only checks that the two known names are present, so it does not catch the miss. Nothing else covers this: ledger-interest.db.test.ts and line-status.db.test.ts each look only at their own migration's NOWAIT loop. The two-line style is common. There are 24 two-line USING ERRCODE raises across 8 migrations (the finding said 13, but that miscount only understates it), including this migration's preflight at lines 67-68, 71-72 and 75-76. Limits: both lock loops that exist today, in 20261109090000 and 20261110090000, are one-line, found and quoted in the runbook, so nothing escapes the guard now. The gap is in how well the guard protects later migrations, so the severity stays nit. The probe is removed, the clone is deleted, and the progress record is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/6af08ef9-734c-5d6d-a787-51ade7156d78/scratchpad/progress/i126d-sk-db-RV-DB1-1.md.
